title: Australia Should Work With China, Not Try to Contain It
gist: The author critiques The Australian's Greg Sheridan for advocating full deference to U.S. military power (via AUKUS minister Richard Marles and the HMAS Stirling base) and for proposing that the U.S. and Australia draft 'common battle plans' against China as 'the only candidate for adversary,' framing this as an argument to contain rather than work with China.

themes.theme: Critique of hawkish Australia-U.S.-China containment stance

insights.claim: Greg Sheridan, foreign editor of The Australian, argues Australia should fully embrace American military power, stating he would rather entrust Australia's security to the U.S. Navy than to the Albanese government.
insights.speaker: Kym Davey
insights.so_what: Represents a hawkish faction of Australian foreign-policy commentary pushing for deeper, more explicit U.S. military dependence, a viewpoint relevant to gauging domestic political support for AUKUS and U.S. basing arrangements.
insights.quote: “Frankly,” he writes, “I’d much rather entrust Australia’s security to the U.S. Navy than to the Albanese government.”

insights.claim: Sheridan's commentary centers on the need to support the U.S. Navy base at HMAS Stirling, arguing Australia should not pretend Stirling is an Australian military base since the country 'actively and happily' shelters under the U.S. extended nuclear umbrella.
insights.speaker: Kym Davey
insights.so_what: Signals ongoing debate over the true operational control and sovereignty of HMAS Stirling as a U.S.-Australia basing arrangement, a point of friction relevant to AUKUS submarine basing plans.
insights.quote: He claims we don’t need to pretend that Stirling is an Australian military base because “we actively and happily shelter under the U.S. extended nuclear umbrella.”

insights.claim: Sheridan proposes that the U.S. and Australia should draw up 'common battle plans' to prepare for conflict with China, described as 'the only candidate for adversary.'
insights.speaker: Kym Davey
insights.so_what: Explicit advocacy for joint U.S.-Australia war planning against China represents an escalatory policy position in Australian discourse; tracking how much traction this view gains among Australian policymakers is a leading indicator for Australia-China relations and defense spending trajectories.
insights.quote: Sheridan proposes that the U.S. and Australia should now draw up “common battle plans” to prepare for conflict with “the only candidate for adversary – China”

insights.claim: The author frames Sheridan's stance as praising Defence/AUKUS Minister Richard Marles for 'kowtowing' to the U.S. military and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, implying the author views this containment-oriented posture critically rather than endorsing it.
insights.speaker: Kym Davey
insights.so_what: The author's critical framing signals a counter-current in Australian debate pushing back against full U.S. military alignment, suggesting political contestation over AUKUS and China policy that could affect Australia's defense posture continuity.
insights.quote: Marles is a good fit for the job at hand: kowtowing to the U.S. military and its boss, the belligerent Pete Hegseth.
